mainEntity.name: How much does a Volvo XC90 T8 engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A Volvo XC90 T8 engine replacement typically costs £5,500-£9,500 for a rebuilt unit supply-only, with fitted prices ranging from £7,000-£12,000 depending on labour rates and ERAD condition. The B4204T35 is the most common T8 engine in UK XC90s. Used engines: £2,200-£5,500. Reconditioned: £4,200-£9,000. Rebuilt with warranty: £5,500-£12,000. Fitting labour: 12-18 hours at £65-£100/hr. ERAD replacement adds £4,500-£6,500 if required.

mainEntity.name: What is ERAD failure and how much does it cost to fix?

acceptedAnswer.text: ERAD (Electric Rear Axle Drive) is the electric motor on the rear axle of the XC90 T8 - a known weak point of the car. Symptoms include intermittent electric motor engagement, loss of all-wheel drive, warning messages like 'Reduced performance' and 'Hybrid system failure'. Clutch pack repair: £1,700-£2,500. Complete ERAD replacement: £4,500-£9,500. Volvo may assist on a case-by-case basis for cars with full service history.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Volvo XC90 T8?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on the vehicle's value and what has failed. For a 2017-2021 XC90 T8 worth £14,000-£45,000, a £5,500-£9,500 rebuilt engine is usually worthwhile if the car is otherwise sound. However, ERAD failure is more common than engine failure - if the ERAD has failed, replacing just the ERAD unit (£4,500-£6,500) is usually the better option. Cars worth £25,000+: rebuilt engine with warranty is recommended. Cars worth £15,000-£25,000: evaluate both options. ERAD failure: repair or replace ERAD, not the engine. Early cars (2015-2017): avoid unless ERAD has been replaced.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of Volvo XC90 T8 engine problems?

acceptedAnswer.text: Common signs include loss of power (supercharger failure), cold-start rattle (timing chain issues), 'Reduced engine performance' warnings, and excessive oil consumption. For ERAD issues specifically, look for intermittent electric motor engagement, loss of rear-wheel drive, and hybrid system warnings. Loss of low-end power: supercharger clutch issue. Rattling on cold start: timing chain tensioner wear. Warning messages: hybrid system or reduced performance. Oil consumption: piston ring wear on higher-mileage units.

mainEntity.name: Is the Volvo XC90 T8 Twin Engine reliable?

acceptedAnswer.text: The petrol engine itself is reasonably reliable, but the T8's hybrid systems - particularly the ERAD unit - have a poor reliability record. Early cars (2015-2017) are the most affected, with Volvo making ERAD improvements from 2018. The facelifted cars from 2020 on (badged 'Recharge') are considered a relatively safe bet. ERAD is the primary reliability concern. Supercharger clutch and seal failure are also common. The 2.0-litre Drive-E petrol engine itself is generally robust. Extended warranty is highly recommended for T8 ownership.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the XC90 T8 and the D5/B5 diesel?

acceptedAnswer.text: The T8 is a plug-in hybrid with a 2.0-litre twin-charged petrol engine and an electric rear motor, producing 303-335 hp from the petrol engine plus 87 hp from the electric motor. The D5/B5 are diesel mild-hybrids with no plug-in capability. The D5/B5 cars are a better bet in terms of dependability, but come with higher running costs and motor tax. T8: PHEV, 303-335 hp petrol + 87 hp electric, up to 32-mile electric range. D5/B5: Diesel mild-hybrid, no plug-in, lower complexity. T8: Higher performance, lower running costs if regularly charged. D5/B5: More dependable, simpler systems.

historyTimeline.h2: Volvo XC90 T8 Twin Engine PHEV - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The T8 Twin Engine was introduced with the second-generation (SPA) Volvo XC90 in 2015, combining Volvo's 2.0-litre Drive-E four-cylinder petrol engine with an electric rear axle drive (ERAD) to create a plug-in hybrid powertrain. It was the first hybrid variant of a VEA engine, using an electric rear axle drive for both electric propulsion and AWD capabilities. The T8 badge has undergone several power upgrades and battery capacity increases over its production life.

milestones.description: B4204T28, 2.0-litre supercharged and turbocharged petrol, 318 hp - original XC90 T8 launch engine, 9.2 kWh battery, 25-mile electric range
B4204T34, 2.0-litre supercharged and turbocharged petrol, 303 hp - lower-power variant for select markets
B4204T35, 2.0-litre supercharged and turbocharged petrol, 320 hp - revised engine with improved torque delivery
B4204T39 Polestar, 2.0-litre supercharged and turbocharged petrol, 333 hp - Polestar Engineered performance variant
B4204T48 Polestar, 2.0-litre supercharged and turbocharged petrol, 318 hp - revised Polestar variant with 348 hp peak
Battery upgrade to 18.6 kWh, electric range increased to 32 miles, badging changed to "Recharge"
B4204T49 Polestar, 2.0-litre supercharged and turbocharged petrol, 335 hp - final Polestar variant
B4204T56, 2.0-litre supercharged and turbocharged petrol, 310 hp - latest T8 AWD variant

commonProblems.h2: Volvo XC90 T8 Twin Engine PHEV Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Volvo XC90 T8 Twin Engine is a sophisticated plug-in hybrid that combines a 2.0-litre twin-charged petrol engine with an electric rear axle drive (ERAD). While the Drive-E petrol engine is broadly reliable, the hybrid-specific components - particularly the ERAD system - have well-documented failure patterns. Rebuilt engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing the original failure point, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: ERAD (Electric Rear Axle Drive) Failure - The Most Common Volvo XC90 T8 Problem
problems.rootCause: The ERAD unit (Electric Rear Axle Drive) - effectively the electric motor on the rear axle - is a known weak point of the XC90 T8. Heat, insufficient lubrication and metal debris gradually wear down bearings and retaining rings. When the retaining ring breaks, failure can spread into the electric motor itself, causing costs to escalate significantly. A 2017 XC90 T8 owner reported ERAD failure at under 72,000 miles with a dealer quote of $12,000.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Clutch pack replacement only (if caught early)
Supply & fit rebuilt engine + ERAD unit, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: If both engine and ERAD have failed

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical 2015-2020 XC90 T8 is worth £12,000-£45,000 depending on mileage and condition. For a sub-£15,000 example, ERAD replacement at £4,500-£6,500 may approach 30-40% of vehicle value. For cars valued above £25,000, the repair is typically justified. Volvo has been known to assist with ERAD replacement on a case-by-case basis for cars with full service history.
problems.recommendation: ERAD failure is the single most common and expensive issue facing XC90 T8 owners. We strongly recommend avoiding early (pre-2018) cars unless the ERAD unit has been replaced recently. For current owners, an extended warranty is highly recommended - ERAD replacement costs dwarf the price of cover, with factory extension plans available from approximately £799 for four years. If the ERAD has failed and you plan to keep the car, a specialist ERAD replacement at £4,500-£6,500 is significantly cheaper than dealer prices (£7,000-£9,500).
problems.cta: -> Compare Volvo XC90 T8 ERAD replacement costs

problems.h4: Supercharger & Turbocharger Failure - Volvo XC90 T8 Twin-Charged System
problems.rootCause: The roots-type supercharger has internally lubricated bearings that eventually fail. The supercharger clutch can fail to engage, requiring the whole unit to be replaced. T8 supercharger seals can also fail, hampering performance. The timing system can also experience issues, presenting as cold-start rattle and fault codes.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt unit with upgraded components

problems.vehicleValueCheck: For a 2017-2021 XC90 T8 worth £14,000-£45,000, a £1,800-£3,000 supercharger replacement is a sensible repair. The engine itself is generally robust - the supercharger is the primary weak point.
problems.recommendation: For XC90 T8 owners experiencing supercharger issues, a supercharger replacement (not a full engine) is usually the right call if caught early. The engine itself is generally robust; the supercharger is the primary weak point. If the engine has suffered consequential damage from supercharger failure, a rebuilt unit with warranty becomes the better option.
problems.cta: -> Compare Volvo XC90 T8 supercharger replacement costs

problems.h4: Hybrid Battery Degradation - Volvo XC90 T8 PHEV
problems.rootCause: The lithium-ion battery pack (9.2 kWh in early cars, 18.6 kWh from 2021) degrades over time. Battery degradation leads to reduced electric range, "Reduced performance" warnings, and eventually complete failure triggering multiple alarming messages.
problems.vehicleValueCheck: Battery replacement at £4,000-£6,500 is significant. For a 2015-2018 XC90 T8 worth £12,000-£25,000, this may represent 20-40% of vehicle value. For newer cars, the cost is more easily justified.
problems.recommendation: Hybrid battery degradation is inevitable with age. For early T8 models (2015-2018), factor battery replacement into ownership costs. A full battery pack replacement from a specialist (£4,000-£6,500) is significantly cheaper than dealer prices. Consider an extended warranty that covers the hybrid battery - this can be cost-effective for high-mileage owners.
problems.cta: -> Compare Volvo XC90 T8 hybrid battery replacement costs

finalCta.h4: Don't Let ERAD or Engine Failure Write Off Your Volvo XC90 T8
finalCta.paragraph: The XC90 T8 is a premium PHEV with complex hybrid systems - ERAD failure, supercharger wear and battery degradation are the three main cost risks. A rebuilt engine with upgraded components and a 12-month warranty, combined with specialist ERAD or battery replacement, is often the most cost-effective long-term solution.
